questions.:question/problem:
Calculate the integral $$
\displaystyle \int x{8}^{3{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=3{x}^{2}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x\,⟹\,\frac{1}{6}\text{d}u=x\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{8}^{3{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & =\int {8}^{3{x}^{2}}\cdot x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {8}^{u}\cdot \frac{1}{6}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\int {8}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\frac{{8}^{u}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡8}+C \\  & =\frac{{8}^{3{x}^{2}}}{6\operatorname{ln}⁡8}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the integral $$
\displaystyle \int {x}^{2}{4}^{{x}^{3}/5}\,\text{d}x.
$$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u=\frac{{x}^{3}}{5}.$ Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{5}{x}^{2}\,⟹\,\frac{5}{3}\text{d}u={x}^{2}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}{4}^{{x}^{3}/5}\,\text{d}x & =\int {4}^{{x}^{3}/5}\cdot {x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {4}^{u}\cdot \frac{5}{3}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{3}\int {4}^{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5\cdot {4}^{u}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C \\  & =\frac{5\cdot {4}^{{x}^{3}/5}}{3\operatorname{ln}⁡4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.:question/problem:
Find an antiderivative.

$$
\int 4 \cdot 5^{2 - x^{3}} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

You may use $\int 5^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u=\frac{5^{u}}{\ln{\left(5 \right)}}+C$.

{{answer}} $+C$
questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=2 - x^{3}$. Then $\mathrm{d}u=(- 3 x^{2})\,\mathrm{d}x$.

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int 4 \cdot 5^{2 - x^{3}} x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\int 5^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the supplied primitive:

$$
- \frac{4}{3}\left(\int 5^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=- \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{5^{u}}{\ln{\left(5 \right)}}\right)+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
- \frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{5^{2 - x^{3}}}{\ln{\left(5 \right)}}\right)+C.
$$

\int 2^{u}\,\mathrm{d}u.

canonical_example.:question/worked-solution:
Let's introduce the new variable $u= 1-x^4.$ Differentiating gives 

$$
\dfrac{ \textrm{d}u}{ \textrm{d}x} = -4x^3\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x^3 \, \textrm{d}x = -\dfrac{1}{4} \textrm{d}u.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int {x^3\,{3^{1-x^4}} }\, \textrm{d}x 
&=\int {{3^{1-x^4}}\cdot x^3 }\, \textrm{d}x \\[5pt]
&=  \int {3^{u}} \cdot \left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) \textrm{d}u\\[5pt]
                                                     &= -\dfrac{1}{4}\int {3^{u}}  \textrm{d}u\\[5pt]
                                                     &=  -\dfrac{1}{4}\cdot\dfrac{3^{u}}{\ln 3} + C\\[5pt]
                                                     &=   -\dfrac{3^{1-x^4}}{4\ln 3}+ C.
\end{aligned}
$$
